title: Competing Consumers

validation.research: Four primary references: Hohpe/Woolf Enterprise Integration Patterns defines Competing Consumers on a shared point-to-point channel; Microsoft documents concurrent queue processing and operational choices; RabbitMQ documents distinct consumer/publisher acknowledgments, bounded outstanding deliveries and connection-loss requeue; Apache Kafka documents conventional consumer-group partition assignment and committed progress. No existing canonical article found; new ID competing-consumers. Consumer groups and shared subscriptions are qualified implementation arrangements, not blanket aliases. Messaging and Integration is the single primary home because the essential collaboration is interchangeable receivers sharing one logical work stream. Publish-Subscribe, Producer-Consumer, Queue-Based Load Leveling and Idempotent Receiver distinctions are explicit. Idempotency does not imply order independence, and delivery ownership does not imply exactly-once external effects.

example_limits: New canonical competing-consumers article, no existing article ID replaced. Competing Consumers is the established Hohpe/Woolf name; shared subscription and consumer group are implementation arrangements, not invented aliases. One primary home Messaging and Integration, as its eleventh completed member. Original thumbnail-job context and bounded sequential Python3.10+ delivery model; one finite tuple of distinct nonempty job IDs, trusted registered consumers A/B, one outstanding delivery each. Explicit scripted interleaving, not real threads/processes or a broker. A receivesJ1/token1, B receivesJ2/token2; B acknowledgesJ2 then receives/acknowledgesJ3/token3 while A still holdsJ1. Explicit disconnectA retires delivery1 and returnsJ1; B receivesJ1/token4, stale token1 acknowledgment is rejected and token4 acknowledged. Logical identity survives redelivery; prior external effect is unknown. Drained means no ready/inflight deliveries, not verified business success. No thumbnail execution, actual parallelism, network, durability, automatic detection/timer, retry limit, transaction/effect store or duplicate-effect prevention. Tokens protect modeled lifecycle only, not external writes or authorization. Kafka conventional partition-group context differs from per-message queue scheduling. Scenarios, simulator and diagrams are original teaching material.
